prompt: One inventory service has a stable typed API. A legacy dashboard requires p95 for complete lookups at or below 20 ms; measured p95 is 12 ms directly and 45 ms through the tested MCP adapter. An unmodified new client connects only to a compatible MCP server and accepts a 200 ms p95 ceiling. Its owner will not maintain a custom client translation layer. Both need the same authoritative inventory operation. Which integration fits these demonstrated requirements?

options.text: Move both clients to the tested MCP adapter for one shared protocol, and ask the dashboard team to relax its latency requirement.
Build a separate inventory implementation for the MCP client, then synchronize its business rules with the typed service.
Keep only the typed API for both clients, and translate the new client’s MCP tool requests inside its own custom client code.
Keep the dashboard on the typed API and expose the same service through MCP for the new client; validate both boundaries.

feedback.reason: The consumers have different demonstrated boundaries: the tested MCP route misses the dashboard’s p95 ceiling, while the new client explicitly needs MCP. Reuse one authoritative service behind a direct API and a client-appropriate protocol adapter.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A shared business operation can support different consumer interfaces without duplicating its implementation. Protocol choice must fit each consumer’s interoperability and complete-route latency requirements.
details.scenarioApplication: The direct 12 ms route meets the dashboard’s 20 ms p95 ceiling; the tested 45 ms MCP adapter does not. The new client has an explicit MCP interface requirement and a 200 ms p95 ceiling.
details.errorCorrection: A universal protocol migration violates one proven constraint, while a duplicate business implementation creates drift. Retain one service and validate its two transport/contract boundaries.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If a revised adapter later meets the dashboard’s p95 ceiling, consolidation can be reevaluated. Current measurements support the split, not a permanent claim that MCP is always slower.
details.transfer: Separate shared domain behavior from consumer-specific interface requirements and compare end-to-end measurements before standardizing every client.

messages.text: The measured 45 ms adapter route exceeds the dashboard’s explicit 20 ms p95 ceiling; protocol uniformity does not justify changing that requirement.
Both clients need the same authoritative operation. A second inventory implementation adds rule synchronization and drift without meeting a distinct domain need.

The new client requires a compatible MCP tool surface. A custom client translation layer shifts that missing protocol implementation into the client rather than providing the required supported boundary.
